extracted.intended_audience: USPTO management, Congressional stakeholders, policy makers, and other readers of the USPTO Performance and Accountability Report (interested public and oversight bodies)
extracted.subtask_description: Performance, financial, and program-management criteria for USPTO patent operations, fee collections, budgeting, and internal controls as presented in the USPTO FY2016 Performance and Accountability Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee schedule and payment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain exclusive rights, a patent holder must pay maintenance fees at three separate intervals: 3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years from the date a patent is issued. Failure to pay these fees results in the lapse of patent protection and the rights provided by a patent are no longer enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fees can be paid during the “window period,” the six-month period preceding each due date. Additionally, a maintenance fee can be paid, with a surcharge, during the “grace period,” the 6-month period immediately following each due date. If a maintenance fee has not been paid in a timely manner and the owner wants rights reinstated, a petition and proper fees are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees revenue recognition and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees are recognized immediately as earned revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluctuations in both the timing of renewal payments and the rates of renewal may have a significant impact on total earned revenue. The USPTO closely monitors payment behaviors (both rates of renewal and timing of payment) to forecast maintenance fee revenue because renewals help recoup costs incurred during the initial patent process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent renewal rate metrics (first/second/third stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal rates are reported for three stages (first stage = end of 3rd year after issue; second stage = end of 7th year; third stage = end of 11th year) showing percentages by issue year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing patent renewal rates, trends are examined year-to-year; preliminary data may be noted (e.g., 2012, 2008, 2004). The decision to renew is influenced by many factors including Federal court decisions, IP budgets, perceived value of the patent, and the economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major patent fee components and revenue share
rubrics_metrics.description: Major components of earned revenue from patent operations are maintenance fees, initial application fees for filing/search/examination, and issue fees; these account for approximately 83 percent of total patent income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee-type breakdown (maintenance, filing/search/examination, issue, extensions of time, PCT, services, other) is used to understand revenue composition and the relative importance of maintenance fees (largest source).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filings as predictor of fee revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Application filing fee revenue and the number of applications filed are tracked and compared year-over-year; increases in filings contribute to increased fee revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: application fee revenue earned upon filing increased from $103.5M in FY2015 to $105.5M in FY2016 while applications rose from 618,062 to 650,411. The President’s Budget projects further increases in filings, which will contribute to budgetary resources and earned fee revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee revenue linked to patents issued and allowance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue fee revenue is correlated with the number of patents issued and the patent allowance rate; increases in issued patents typically increase issue fee revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: earned issue fee revenue increased from $268.7M in FY2015 to $274.2M in FY2016 with patents issued increasing from 322,448 to 334,107—reflecting production and allowance rate trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting cost recovery requirement under the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the America Invents Act (AIA) fee-setting authority, the USPTO must set certain fees to recover the aggregate estimated cost of Patent and Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) operations and USPTO administrative services that support Patent operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To implement this, the USPTO may issue NPRMs (notice of proposed rulemaking) and final rules to set or increase certain patent fees so fee schedules are responsive to stakeholder concerns while allowing recovery of aggregate estimated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness targets for patent examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide timely examination of patent applications — reduce average time to first office action to 10 months and average total pendency to 20 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: average time from filing until an examiner’s initial determination on patentability = time to first office action; average time from filing until the application is issued as a patent or abandoned = total pendency. These are explicit performance targets in the USPTO 2014–2018 Strategic Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance quality of patent examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the quality of patent examination as a strategic objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality is a primary strategic goal aligned with other measures (e.g., pendency, appeals) and is to be tracked with associated performance indicators under the agency’s strategic performance framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve patent appeal and post-grant processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve patent appeal and post-grant processes as a strategic objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This objective is part of the strategic plan and links to performance measures for PTAB and post-grant activities aimed at timely and effective resolution of appeals and post-grant matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced Scorecard alignment with performance indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Align agency goals and objectives with associated performance indicators using a Balanced Scorecard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Balanced Scorecard provides meaningful information on the status and performance of every initiative in the strategic plan and strengthens capacity by focusing on a specific set of goals and steps to reach them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow composition and adjustments for federal entity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash flow is measured by components: operations, investing, and financing, with adjustments made for non-cash items (e.g., depreciation) and timing differences (e.g., accrued payroll, deferred revenue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: depreciation and accrued payroll increase net cash provided by operations (non-cash expenses), while decreases in deferred revenue can increase net income without a corresponding increase in cash flow; other adjustments (changes in accounts payable) affect net cash provided by operational activities. Statement of Cash Flows is audited and presented for additional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary resource management and fee reserve fund authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage budgetary resources and appropriations, including use of the Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund allowed by the AIA to deposit fees collected in excess of appropriated levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO tracks temporarily unavailable fee collections when not appropriated authority to spend all fees collected. Prior-year collections and special fund unavailable receipts (e.g., OBRA 1990 deposit) are tracked as cumulative unavailable fee collections held at Treasury until appropriated. Operating reserve management and transfers follow appropriations and reprogramming agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program cost drivers and allocation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Program costs are broken down into direct and allocated costs with personnel services and benefits typically the largest component (approximately 63% of total program costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs attributable to Patent, Trademark, and IP protection business areas represent ~81.5% of total USPTO costs. Allocated costs are determined using activity-based cost accounting; changes in staffing or pay rates directly impact total program costs year-to-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent product cost distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent program costs are distributed across patent products (e.g., utility patents, 371 filings, PTAB, PCT, design, plant, other) with percentages reported (example: utility 71.6%, 371 filing 17.7%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost percentages are based on direct and indirect costs allocated to patent operations and are a function of the volume of applications processed in each product area; tracking by product informs resource allocation and fee-setting considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement requirements for the Attaché Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attaché Program should have baselines and targets associated with its quantitative performance measures to permit assessment of program performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found that although the program established goals and six performance measures (e.g., number of training/public awareness programs, number of officials trained), none included baselines or targets. USPTO concurred and will increase data collection to establish baselines and targets, while noting that quantitative measures should not be the sole measure of effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls for telework equipment and asset management
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and maintain controls over laptops, printers, and other telework equipment used by full-time teleworkers, including inventory and separation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG recommended improvements: conduct inventories (though annual physical inventory may be impractical for dispersed teleworkers), ensure adequate segregation of duties over quarterly inventory certification, ensure completion of separation clearance forms, and upgrade asset management system to enable remote, real-time confirmation of assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement best practices for noncompetitive contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Noncompetitive contract awards must be properly justified, approved, and documented following best practices (OFPP, FAR, Commerce Acquisition Manual, and USPTO policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found inadequate justification for sole source awards and weak acquisition planning. Recommended actions include improving market research and surveys to maximize competition, properly document price reasonableness determinations, ensure procurements are reviewed/approved at appropriate levels, and require contracting officers to document sole source justifications and price analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and attendance controls for patent examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement controls to prevent and detect time and attendance abuse among patent examiners, including ensuring a sufficient digital footprint for claimed work hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG analysis identified substantial unsupported hours across sampled examiners. USPTO actions include training, updated policies, added controls, tools for supervisors, and development of systems to improve workforce management and detection of unsupported time entries.
